title: Hotteok: Chewy Korean Pancakes with Brown Sugar, Cinnamon and Peanuts
summary: Soft, chewy yeasted pancakes filled with brown sugar, cinnamon and peanuts, pressed flat and fried until crisp and golden.
equipment: flat metal spatula or hotteok press

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Stir the sugar and yeast into the warm milk in the large bowl. Add both flours, the cornflour and salt and beat with the wooden spoon for 2-3 min into a very sticky, stretchy dough. The rice flour gives the chewy texture.

steps.title: Let it rise twice
steps.text: Cover and leave somewhere warm for 1.5-2 h until doubled. Beat it down with the spoon, cover again and leave for about 1 h more until puffy.

steps.title: Mix the filling
steps.text: Combine the dark brown sugar, chopped peanuts, cinnamon and salt in the small bowl.

steps.title: Fill and seal
steps.text: With oiled or floured hands, divide the dough into 10 pieces. Flatten one in your palm into a cupped 10 cm round, spoon in 2 packed tablespoons of filling, then pull the edges up and pinch them tightly together. Set seam side down on a floured surface and repeat. A firm seal keeps the melting sugar inside.

steps.title: Press and fry
steps.text: Heat about 2 tbsp oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat. Add 2 or 3 balls seam side down and flatten each straight away with the spatula to about 10 cm across. Turn the heat to medium and cook for 3-4 min until crisp and golden, then flip and cook 3-4 min more until springy to the touch.

steps.title: Fry the rest
steps.text: Wipe the pan clean and add fresh oil for each batch. Let the pancakes rest for a few minutes before eating, as the filling is very hot.

tips: A common mistake is adding extra flour because the dough is sticky; it should be very soft, so oil your hands instead.
Press the pancakes flat as soon as they hit the pan, before the bottom sets.
Keep the heat at medium after pressing so the inside cooks before the outside darkens.
Walnuts or mixed seeds can replace the peanuts.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten warm. Cool leftovers fully and freeze in an airtight container for up to 1 month; reheat at 180 °C (160 °C fan) for 8-10 min.
